title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the 'equation des lacets' material that follows La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is working with three things: a profinite fundamental group pi of an orbifold of type M_{0,3}/M_{1,1}; a larger group G containing pi with index 2; and an arithmetic/Teichmüller extension M (written M(0) ≃ Pi_Q^~ ≃ Gamma_Q^~, a Galois–Teichmüller-type group).

The notation:
- rho and sigma are the torsion elements of orders 3 (or 6) and 2 (or 4). They correspond to the elliptic points j=0 and j=1728 of the modular orbifold, i.e. to the generators of hat{SL_2(Z)} or hat{PSL_2(Z)} ≃ Z/2 * Z/3 completed.
- N_rho^* and N_sigma^* are normalizer-type groups of the cyclic subgroups L_rho = <rho> and L_sigma = <sigma> inside M.
- Z^!_{rho,sigma} is the subgroup normalizing both. By (125) it is a semidirect product M(0).L_0^pi.
- L_0^pi = l_0^{hat Z} is the procyclic inertia (loop) subgroup at the cusp 0. It has index 2 in L_0^G = epsilon_0^{hat Z}, with l_0 = epsilon_0^2 (eq. 127).
- gamma_{rho,sigma} = Z^!/L_0^pi ≃ M(0) ≃ Pi_Q^~.

On the previous page Grothendieck defined two homomorphisms (123), Z^! → N_rho^*/{±1} and Z^! → N_sigma^*. Each is defined by choosing a conjugating element, which is only determined modulo something.

On this page he restricts both homomorphisms to the inertia subgroup L_0^pi.
1. By the characterization (122), the induced map L_0^pi → N_rho^*/{±1} is trivial. The reason given is that the relevant element is only defined up to an ambiguity mod pi^.
2. The induced map L_0^pi → N_sigma^* factors through L_0^pi / L_0^{pi_0} ≃ Z/2Z. Here pi_0 is an index-2 subgroup of pi, and b is only defined mod pi_0^.
3. The value b on the generator b_0 is characterized by b ∈ N_sigma^* and b ≡ b_0 (mod pi_0). Since b = -1 satisfies these conditions, the generator goes to -1, the central element (sigma^2 = -1 in SL_2).
4. Introducing the canonical generator of mu = mu_2 ≃ L_0^pi/L_0^{pi_0}, he obtains an embedding (128) mu ↪ N_sigma^* sending the generator to -1. He also obtains a commutative square (129) relating L_0^pi ↪ Z^! and mu ↪ N_sigma^*.

What this serves. Passing to the quotient by L_0^pi (and by ±1), the next page obtains canonical homomorphisms (130) gamma_{rho,sigma} = Gamma_Q^~ → N_rho^*/{±1} and → N_sigma^*/{±1}. These are sections of the natural projections. They give semidirect decompositions (131):
- N_rho^*/{±1} ≃ gamma ⋉ Z/3, with action through the quadratic character epsilon_3 (the cyclotomic character mod 3);
- N_sigma^*/{±1} ≃ gamma ⋉ Z/2, with the mod-4 character epsilon_2.

In modern terms, this is the computation of the Galois/GT action on the normalizers of the finite (torsion) subgroups of the profinite modular group. These subgroups are the decomposition groups at the orbifold points with extra automorphisms (CM points j=0, 1728). The result is 'Galois sections' attached to these points, with the action on the stabilizers given by cyclotomic characters.
errors: The justification for triviality of L_0^pi → N_rho^*/{±1} is only sketched ('car à un terme ... près n'est défini que mod pi^'). It relies on the characterization (122), which is not on this page, so it cannot be checked here.

Notation is loose. mu (= mu_2 = {±1}) is identified with L_0^pi/L_0^{pi_0} ≃ Z/2Z. In (128) the source element is written '1' (overwritten) mapping to -1; if mu = {±1} multiplicatively, the generator should read -1 ↦ -1.

On the next page, the action on L_sigma/{±1} ≃ Z/2Z is said to be via a quadratic character epsilon_2. But any action on Z/2 is trivial, so the character can only be meaningful on L_sigma ≃ Z/4 before dividing by ±1. This is a minor imprecision, not on this page.

ideas.what: Restriction of the conjugation/section homomorphisms attached to the torsion points rho, sigma to the cusp inertia L_0^pi. The rho-part is trivial; the sigma-part factors through Z/2 and sends the generator to the central element -1.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of inertia at a cusp with the decomposition groups/normalizers of torsion elements in the profinite modular group (orbifold points of M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Studied for GT/Galois actions on torsion of profinite mapping class groups by Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (late 1990s) and B. Collas (2010s); unsure of exact attribution of this specific lemma

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphisms gamma_{rho,sigma} ≃ Gamma_Q^~ → N_rho^*/{±1}, N_sigma^*/{±1} that are sections, giving semidirect decompositions with action via cyclotomic characters mod 3 and mod 4 (prepared on this page, completed on the next).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT sections at the elliptic (CM) orbifold points j=0, j=1728 of M_{1,1}; GT action on torsion conjugacy classes via cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: B. Collas (action of a GT group on torsion elements of genus-one mapping class groups); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps; Nakamura

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes how the (GT/Galois-type) extension acts on normalizers of the order-3 and order-2/4 torsion subgroups, and how cusp inertia sits inside them. This yields canonical sections and cyclotomic-character actions. It anticipates later work on GT actions on torsion elements and inertia stacks of profinite mapping class groups (Collas; Collas–Maugeais), apparently without those authors knowing of this manuscript.
missed.quote: l'hom induit L_0^pi → N_sigma^* se factorise par L_0^pi/L_0^{pi_0} ≃ Z/2Z ... (128) mu ↪ N_sigma^*, 1 ↦ -1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the 'torsion/CM-point' part of the GT program. The explicit description of the cusp-inertia compatibility (129) could be compared with the known results on GT-equivariance of torsion conjugacy classes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in a longer computation. The underlying statement — Galois/GT acts on torsion stabilizers of the profinite modular group through cyclotomic characters and gives sections at CM points — is known in later literature. The page mainly documents that Grothendieck carried out this analysis himself, including the compatibility with cusp inertia.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription duplicates a line. The image reads roughly: 'est trivial (car à un terme près n'est défini que mod pi^), tandis que l'hom induit L_0^pi → N_sigma^* se factorise par L_0^pi/L_0^{pi_0} ≃ Z/2Z (car b à un terme près n'est défini que de mu mod pi_0^)'.
'Sa valeur b/sur b_0 est caractérisée par les conditions': 'caractérisée' is written over a struck word (likely 'définie'), not '{+caractérisée+}' replacing 'déterminée'.

'Donc puisqu'il y a lieu d'introduire...' is more plausibly 'Donc, puisqu'il y a lieu d'introduire aussi, quitte à l'oublier en route, le mu-générateur canonique, on voit que' — not 'connaissons que'.
In (128) the source element is overwritten (looks like '4' corrected to '1' or '-1'). The intended map is the generator of mu ↦ -1.
First display: L_0^pi → N_rho^*/{±1} (the '{±1}' is partly overwritten in the image).
